title: What Is a Tech Recruiter? (September 2026)
summary: Find out what tech recruiters do, how much they earn, and why fractional recruiting works better for startups in September 2026.
body_markdown:
You’ve likely wondered what exactly[tech recruiters](https://www.dover.com/) do and whether they’re worth working with when you’re trying to build your engineering team. The challenge comes down to understanding their role and figuring out whether a tech recruiter or fractional recruiter can help you find the right technical talent, without breaking your budget or wasting your time. So let’s break down where tech recruiters can help you, the cost of hiring one, and what your decision should be based on as a startup founder.


**TLDR:**


-


Tech recruiters specialize in technical roles and earn $52k to $150k+ depending on experience and location.


-


Strong recruiters combine technical fluency with cultural assessment skills to find quality candidates fast.


-


Fractional recruiters offer cost-effective alternatives to traditional 15-25% agency placement fees.


-


Some fractional recruiting marketplaces connect startups with vetted recruiters who work hourly without long-term contracts.


-


Some integrated recruiting tools pair a free ATS with on-demand recruiter access so hiring teams and recruiters share one pipeline from day one.


## What Are Tech Recruiters


Tech recruiters are specialized talent acquisition professionals who focus exclusively on filling technical roles within tech companies. Unlike general recruiters who might work across multiple industries, tech recruiters develop deep expertise in programming languages, software development methodologies, and the specific skill sets required for engineering positions.


Tech recruiters typically specialize in roles like software engineers, data scientists, DevOps engineers, cybersecurity specialists, and technical leadership positions.


For startups especially, working with[startup recruiters](https://www.dover.com/blog/what-is-a-startup-recruiter) who understand the unique challenges of early-stage companies can be the difference between landing top talent and losing candidates to larger companies with more developed recruiting processes.


## Key Responsibilities of Tech Recruiters


Tech recruiters handle a complex set of responsibilities that go far beyond posting job descriptions and scheduling interviews. Their work begins with understanding the technical requirements of each role, which often involves collaborating closely with engineering teams to define the required skills and the ideal candidate profile.


Key responsibilities include:


-


Writing role-specific job descriptions that accurately reflect the technical stack, architecture context, and engineering expectations, not generic listings that could apply to any software role


-


Sourcing through technical channels like Wellfound (formerly AngelList), Dice, LinkedIn, and GitHub, identifying candidates with relevant contributions instead of relying on inbound applications alone


-


Conducting technical phone screens to assess depth of experience in specific languages, frameworks, or systems before passing candidates to engineering teams


-


Coordinating and structuring technical interview loops, including take-home assignments, system design rounds, and panel interviews with appropriate engineering stakeholders


-


Managing offer negotiations for engineering roles, including conversations around base salary, equity, signing bonuses, and remote or hybrid arrangements that candidates in technical fields often weigh carefully


Tech recruiters also serve as market intelligence resources for their clients. They understand current salary trends, know which companies are hiring aggressively, and can provide insights about what motivates technical candidates to make career moves.


Working with recruiters who excel at these core responsibilities can dramatically improve both the speed and quality of technical hires.


## How Tech Recruiters Work


The workflow of successful tech recruiters combines systematic processes with relationship-driven approaches. Most begin each search by conducting a detailed intake session with the hiring team. They spend time understanding team dynamics, technical architecture, and growth plans.


Their sourcing strategies include mining GitHub for developers with relevant contributions, participating in technical communities like Reddit’s programming subreddits, and maintaining relationships with candidates from previous searches.


Screening processes typically involve multiple touchpoints. An initial phone screen focuses on technical background and career motivations, followed by a more detailed technical conversation or a brief coding exercise. The evaluation phase requires tech recruiters to synthesize technical assessments, cultural fit, and practical considerations like salary expectations and timeline.


They present candidates to clients with detailed profiles, including resume, insights about motivation, technical strengths, and potential concerns.


Modern tech recruiters also use technology extensively. They use applicant tracking systems, sourcing tools, and increasingly AI-enhanced tools to handle large candidate volumes well.


Understanding these workflows helps set appropriate expectations and creates better partnerships with recruiting professionals.


## Tech Recruiter Salary Information


Tech recruiter compensation varies widely based on experience level, geographic location, and the types of companies they work with. Understanding these salary ranges can help both aspiring recruiters and companies budgeting for recruiting services.


Level Experience Base Salary (Annual) Total Compensation (with Bonus/Commission)


Entry-Level Tech Recruiter 0-2 years $52,000 to $70,000 +20-40% of base (commissions/bonuses)


Mid-Level Tech Recruiter 3-7 years $70,000 to $95,000 $100,000 to $130,000


Senior Tech Recruiter / Recruiting Manager 7+ years $95,000 to $125,000+ $148,000 to $190,000+


Geographic location has a big impact on these ranges. California tech recruiters, particularly in the San Francisco Bay Area, typically earn[roughly 28% more](https://www.indeed.com/career/technical-recruiter/salaries/CA) than the national average, according to Indeed’s September 2026 data.


Company type also influences earnings. In-house recruiters at major tech companies often receive higher base salaries plus equity compensation. Agency recruiters might have lower bases but higher commission potential.[Fractional recruiters](https://www.dover.com/recruiters) , like those in Dover’s network, work on flexible hourly rates. This often means lower total costs for startups compared to traditional placement fees.


## Finding the Right Tech Recruiter


Selecting the right tech recruiter requires looking at both their technical knowledge and their track record with similar hiring challenges. The best recruiters show genuine understanding of your technology stack, can discuss technical trade-offs intelligently, and have successfully placed candidates in comparable roles.


-


Assess technical fluency: A quality tech recruiter should be able to explain the difference between front-end and back-end development, and understand why certain programming languages might be better suited for specific projects.


-


Track record assessment: Ask for specific examples of challenging searches they’ve completed, particularly those involving similar company stages, or technical requirements.


-


Communication: Recruiters who are slow to respond or don’t provide regular updates will struggle to compete for top talent on your behalf.


-


Cultural assessment skills: Look for recruiters who ask thoughtful questions about your company culture, team working styles, and growth stage challenges.


-


Transparency: Be wary of recruiters who make unrealistic promises about timeline, their fee structure or candidate quality, or who are vague about their sourcing strategies.


For startups, consider recruiters who understand the unique challenges of early-stage companies: someone who appreciates that startups can’t always compete on salary but can offer equity, growth opportunities, and meaningful work.


## Working with Tech Recruiters


Successful partnerships with tech recruiters require clear communication, realistic expectations, and collaborative approaches to the hiring process. The relationship works best when both parties understand their roles and maintain regular communication throughout the search process.


-


**Set clear expectations:**Define the ideal candidate profile in detail, including must-have technical skills, nice-to-have skills, the right experience level, and cultural fit requirements.


-


**Provide context:** Share information about the team structure, current technical challenges, growth plans, and company culture. The more context recruiters have, the better they can represent your opportunity to candidates and assess fit accurately.


-


**Maintain communication:** When recruiters present candidates, provide timely feedback that goes beyond simple yes/no responses.


-


**Define processes:** Great technical candidates often have multiple opportunities, so efficient interview processes and quick decision-making can be competitive advantages. Work with your recruiter to optimize your interview workflow before beginning the search.


-


**Set clear performance metrics:** Discuss how you’ll measure success, what constitutes reasonable progress, and how often you’ll review the search status. Tracking shared recruiting metrics gives both sides a common baseline.


Red flags to watch for include recruiters who submit large numbers of unqualified candidates, fail to provide candidate context, or pressure you to make quick decisions without adequate evaluation time. Quality recruiters focus on fit over volume.


Working closely with experienced recruiters can provide valuable insights about candidate expectations and interview best practices.


## The 2026 Tech Recruiting Environment


Understanding the current market helps explain why the choice of recruiting model matters more than ever. A few structural changes in 2026 are making the case for specialized recruiting partners stronger, not weaker. AI-generated applications have flooded inboxes:[~40% of tech candidates inflate their resumes](https://recruiterflow.com/blog/recruitment-trends/) , with Deloitte’s 2026 report warning that deepfake interviews and AI-written applications are undermining the hiring signals recruiters have historically relied on, according to Recruiterflow’s 2026 recruitment trends analysis. At the same time, internal recruiting teams are stretched thin: recruiting headcount is down about 14% from 2021 levels, yet teams are managing around 40% more open roles and handling 93% more applications per recruiter, according to[National University’s 2026 hiring data](https://www.nu.edu/blog/67-hiring-statistics/) .


The practical consequence for startups is that the window for acting quickly on strong candidates has narrowed. A specialized tech recruiter, particularly one already running active candidate relationships, can reach people who won’t surface through a standard job posting. Skills-based screening is also displacing credential-first filtering, with[70% of employers now using skills-based hiring](https://www.forbes.com/sites/terdawn-deboe/2026/08/10/employers-are-hiring-for-skills-over-degrees-now-ai-is-why/) , up from 65% the year before, and 53% having eliminated degree requirements entirely, according to Forbes citing NACE’s Job Outlook 2026 survey. That change rewards recruiters who can assess technical judgment instead of simply matching resumes to job descriptions.

## FAQs


### When should I consider hiring a tech recruiter instead of recruiting myself?


Consider hiring a tech recruiter if you’re spending more than 10-15 hours per week on recruiting activities, struggling to source qualified technical candidates, or competing against larger companies for the same talent pool. Recruiters are especially valuable when you need to move quickly in competitive markets.


### Can fractional tech recruiters work with our existing hiring tools?


Yes, experienced fractional recruiters typically integrate with your existing ATS and hiring workflows. This creates transparency throughout the process and makes sure no candidates are lost between systems, unlike traditional agencies that often use separate tracking systems.


### Do I need an ATS before bringing in a fractional recruiter?


Strictly speaking, no. A fractional recruiter can start work before an ATS is in place. The cleaner path, though, is to have a shared pipeline system set up first, because without one the recruiter and the hiring team end up tracking candidates in two separate places and spend real time just syncing status. Some fractional recruiting models include ATS access as part of the arrangement, so the recruiter and hiring team work from a single shared system from day one with no coordination lag. If you are evaluating fractional recruiting options, it is worth asking whether pipeline tooling is bundled in or something you need to bring separately.


### What hiring tools do most early-stage and YC startups use?


Most early-stage startups, including YC-backed teams, rely on a lightweight stack: an ATS to manage pipeline, a sourcing tool for outbound outreach (LinkedIn Recruiter Lite or similar), and a scheduling tool to reduce coordination overhead. The common thread is cost sensitivity and speed: founders want tools that work on day one without dedicated recruiting ops support. Dover’s[free ATS](https://www.dover.com/ats) is built for this context: it handles pipeline tracking and integrates directly with fractional recruiters so nothing falls through the cracks as headcount grows.


### What is the best free applicant tracking system for a team just starting to hire?


For teams making their first few hires, the right ATS is one that requires no configuration overhead and doesn’t gate core features behind a paid plan. An ATS built for startups without dedicated recruiting staff tracks candidates, supports collaborative hiring, and connects directly with fractional recruiters if you need sourcing support. The distinction worth drawing: an ATS handles pipeline visibility and process structure, but it doesn’t replace the judgment needed to source and assess technical candidates. If you’re hiring engineers and competing against larger companies, pairing a free ATS with a fractional recruiter who already has active candidate relationships tends to close roles faster than either approach alone.


## Final Thoughts on Working with Tech Recruiters


As of September 2026, the right recruiting model depends on role complexity, hiring volume, and your team’s bandwidth.[Tech recruiters](https://www.dover.com/) , whether traditional agency, in-house, or fractional, work best when they function as part of the team rather than a vendor. Dover is one concrete implementation of that model: a free ATS paired with on-demand fractional recruiters in a single shared system, averaging $2,000 to $7,000 per hire with no retainer or long-term contract required.
